summary: Clearwater NF 40-foot L-4 lookout on Lean-To Ridge, built about 1934 and destroyed in 1963; a 1931 newspaper already names a lookout there.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1963, per firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the 2016 Forest Service list

events.note: Fire on Hemlock Creek and Lean-to Ridge scorched more than 5,000 acres; a newspaper report says the flames advanced toward the Lean-to Ridge Lookout
40-foot L-4 tower; patrol tree platform eight miles southwest

evidence.supports: Location 16 miles east of Pierce in Clearwater County
1934 40-foot L-4 tower; patrol tree platform eight miles southwest; destroyed 1963
evidence.quote: 1934: 40' L-4 tower. Patrol tree platform 8 miles southwest. Destroyed 1963.

evidence.supports: Patrol tree platform eight miles southwest

evidence.quote: A 14x14 cabin design, these were the original, prefabricated live-in lookout

evidence.supports: July 1931 fire on Hemlock Creek and Lean-to Ridge advancing toward the lookout
evidence.quote: The flames were racing up Hemlock creek and advancing toward the Lean-to Ridge Lookout.

evidence.supports: More than 5,000 acres of timber scorched in the 1931 fire
evidence.quote: More than 5000 acres of timber have been scorched by the fast spreading fire on Hemlock creek and Lean-to ridge in the Clearwater forest in northern Idaho

evidence.supports: Destroyed 1963 on the Forest Service list
40-foot L-4 with 1934 build year on the Forest Service list

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the 2016 Forest Service list date the 40-foot L-4 tower to 1934. A July 1931 newspaper, quoted on Forest Lookouts, already names the Lean-to Ridge Lookout. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.

sources.title: Clearwater National Forest Lookouts (list compiled June 2016)

notes_for_editor: Three of the four listings agree on 1934 and 1963. The 1931 fire and the lookout it names come only from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes the Twin Falls Daily News; I did not check the newspaper itself. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so the story leaves staffing out. Today: no source describes the site now, and none gives access. The record's status gone, kind tower and agency match the sources. Facts height_m 12.2 is 40 feet converted; elevation 5,078 ft is in the story but is not a facts key. No new photos. The Forest Service list has a 'None' photo count for this lookout.
